caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Best Buy Co., Inc.
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — E.D. Cal. Sacramento; FCRA/ICRAA discovery pleaded on or about May 29, 2026; Penal Code § 290.46 runs on CCP § 338(a) from the October 2023 use (outer bound October 17, 2026). Inspection demands drafted but unsigned.
note: The September 8, 2026 San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Generate the federal review-draft PDF with internal/scripts/matter39-edca-complaint.py. Unsigned inspection demands: internal/docs/matter-39/INSPECTION_DEMAND_FIRST_ADVANTAGE.md and PERSONNEL_FILE_DEMAND_BEST_BUY.md. May 29, 2026 is FCRA/ICRAA discovery only; Count 3 does not reallege it and uses CCP § 338(a) from October 2023 (outer bound October 17, 2026). Serve the current SOS agent, not 6653 Hopkins Road. Do not treat another employer's report as Best Buy's report.
defendants: Best Buy Co., Inc., a Minnesota corporation with its principal place of business in Richfield, Minnesota, is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report. First Advantage Background Services Corp. is pleaded as Best Buy's CRA from Best Buy's own October 17, 2023 emails; it remains a nonparty discovery source unless Best Buy-specific records support an independent CRA claim. Jose Tapia (GM) and Daisy Calvary are witnesses. Best Buy Stores, L.P. is reserved if the personnel file shows a different employing affiliate.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — Best Buy allegedly took adverse employment action based in whole or in part on the First Advantage report without first providing the report and written Summary of Rights; negligent/willful remedies under §§ 1681o/1681n.

[DISTINCT STATE OMISSION] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — upon denying/ending employment under circumstances in which an investigative report was obtained, Best Buy allegedly failed to advise Plaintiff and supply the CRA name/address at adverse action. Naming First Advantage on the earlier authorization is not the § 1786.40 advice. Pleaded as a different omission from the FCRA pre-adverse failure to avoid § 1786.52(a) same-act duplication.

[I&B ULTIMATE FACTS] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — complaint pleads on information and belief that First Advantage furnished Plaintiff's California-registry information and Best Buy used it for the Tracy employment decision, supported by Best Buy's own written offer, named vendor, same-day screen, and UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparators. Exact source-field wording remains reserved for discovery.
[OMITTED] UCL — limited remedial upside and unnecessary federal standing/remedy side fight.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — reserve unless the actual Best Buy product is an ordinary consumer credit report rather than an investigative employment report.
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED / contract / estoppel — two-year CCP § 335.1 clock from an October 2023 decision closed in October 2025.
[RESERVED] FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), Fair Chance Act / FEHA, and First Advantage vendor claims — add only if the actual forms, exhaustion record, or CRA conduct support them.
key_facts: On Oct. 13, 2023, Best Buy emailed that it had received Plaintiff's application for General Warehouse Worker / 2nd Shift at $22.60, requisition 928556BR. The warehouse is 6653 Hopkins Road, Tracy, CA 95377. On Oct. 17 at 3:47 p.m., Jose Tapia, General Manager, emailed a congratulations offer and required, within 24 hours, Candidate Zone signature, background-check information, and background-check authorization. At 4:22 p.m. Best Buy sent a background-authorization confirmation naming First Advantage Consumer Center. At 4:30 p.m. First Advantage ordered a Best Buy drug test (Q09078711; account BEST BUY 11759586; Quest Modesto is a collection option, not the worksite). Plaintiff accepted the offer and completed the drug screening. On information and belief, that screen came back clean. Best Buy then ceased communication and ghosted him. No pre-adverse letter, adverse letter, or Best Buy report is in the file. Report contents and use are I&B ultimate facts. Supporting basis: written offer, named First Advantage, same-day screen, contemporaneous Megan's Law listing, UPS/FedEx same-consumer comparators, no other basis communicated, and exclusive control of the Best Buy report.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft. Prior signed San Joaquin complaint dated September 8, 2026 was never filed. Proposed forum is E.D. Cal. Sacramento. Serve the current SOS agent. Unsigned §§ 1786.22 / 1198.5 demands are drafted. FCRA/ICRAA discovery is pleaded on or about May 29, 2026. Count 3 does not reallege that date and is timely under CCP § 338(a) from the October 2023 use (outer bound October 17, 2026). Remaining gates: Plaintiff confirmation of the FCRA/ICRAA discovery date, Plaintiff signature, official JS-44 / AO-440, SOS-agent confirmation, and a final hostile audit of every I&B allegation.
damages: Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages including lost employment compensation at the offered $22.60 hourly rate according to proof; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus punitive damages if the statutory showing is met; and remedies authorized by Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A). The offer does not state weekly hours or a start date; those figures are not invented. Diversity AIC is pleaded in the aggregate.
risk: FCRA/ICRAA limitations fight will be inquiry notice: Best Buy named First Advantage on October 17, 2023 and then ghosted him. Those counts plead May 29, 2026 discovery of the process omissions; two years runs to May 29, 2028. Count 3 does not use May 29; it is a CCP § 338(a) three-year statutory claim from the October 2023 use, outer bound October 17, 2026. Do not plead May 29 as when Plaintiff knew he had been harmed. Best Buy will move to compel arbitration on the application-email recital; that is a defense. Merits: vendor identity is documentary; § 290.46 source/use remain I&B with UPS/FedEx comparators. Exact source wording is reserved for the Best Buy-specific report.
